title: Cascade fallback controller for granular SLO violations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a Cascade Fallback Controller that evaluates multiple SLO signals (p50/p95 latency, user-visible error rate, token cost per response, and throughput) across cohorts and tiers, and executes graduated mitigations for canary/A-B/shadow rollouts.

Scope:
- Integrate multi-signal detection with current rollout orchestration: canary traffic slices, A/B buckets, and shadow siphon.
- Implement tiered mitigations: soft throttles, model variant fallback, traffic re-routing to baseline, and scheduled rollback.
- Provide a tunable threshold profile model that supports soft alarms (warning) and hard alarms (evacuate), with decay windows and cohort baselining.

Non-goals:
- Not handling offline on-prem upgrade orchestration (covered by Private team).
- Not replacing existing human-on-call escalation; this is an automated safety-first controller with op notifications.

Acceptance criteria:
- Controller can ingest at least four live signals (latency p95, error rate, tokens-per-response, throughput) from Console telemetry and make decisions within 30s of threshold breach.
- Rollout mitigations are applied in order (throttle -> model fallback -> reroute -> rollback) with configurable delays and can be overridden from Console.
- Post-mitigation metrics show median improvement on the triggering signal within configured SLO windows in >= 80% test runs in the staging harness.
- End-to-end integration test covering canary and shadow traffic scenarios exists in CI (test harness + synthetic traffic), and a playbook for false-positive recovery is documented.

Design notes / unique aspects:
- Cascade approach: when a signal crosses a soft threshold, we first apply non-disruptive mitigations (e.g., reduce canary qps, enable prefix caching) before escalating. Only on hard threshold breach do we perform model fallback or rollback.
- Cost-weighted decisions: token-cost regressions are treated as first-class signals but with a tunable weight — teams can prioritize latency vs cost per their SLAs.
- Cohort-aware baselining: for user cohorts with different latency distributions (mobile vs desktop, EU vs US), thresholds are evaluated relative to cohort baselines to reduce noisy rollbacks.
- Shadow siphoning: when shadow traffic shows degradation, controller can mark a model as "quarantine" and automatic siphoning rate is limited while further telemetry is collected.
- Decay windows and staleness: controller uses sliding windows with decay to avoid reacting to very short spikes; windows are configurable per signal.

Telemetry & metrics (for observability):
- Alerts emitted: warning_engagement, hard_evacuation, mitigations_applied (with type).
- Stored context: snapshot of recent p50/p95, error counts, tokens_avg, throughput, cohort breakdown at time of action.
- Dashboard: per-rollout timeline view with mitigation actions and pre/post metrics.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Over-sensitive thresholds cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: staged deployment of thresholds with A/B testing and synthetic fuzzing, and a protected grace period before hard evacuations.
- Risk: Signal correlation causing oscillation between fallback and restore. Mitigation: hysteresis policies and minimum cool-down between escalations.
- Risk: Cost signals may be gamed by adversarial traffic patterns. Mitigation: cross-signal checks before high-impact actions (e.g., require both token-cost and latency to breach before rollback on some profiles).

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Instrumentation: extend rollout controller to pull structured signals from Console metrics API and tag by cohort — (work: ENG infra + telemetry).
2) Simple rule engine: implement first pass rule engine to map soft/hard thresholds to actions (throttle -> fallback -> reroute -> rollback).
3) Simulation harness: create a synthetic traffic generator that replays production traces under canary and shadow modes to validate tuning.
4) Gradual rollout: enable controller in staging (shadow-only), then opt-in for low-volume customers, then platform-wide.

Links to artifacts:
- Design doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.local/rollouts/cascade-fallback-controller
- Simulation harness (repo): https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts-sim/pull/118
- Initial prototype PR (infra): https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-controller/pull/402

Notes on threshold tuning model:
- Default profiles: latency-first, cost-aware, conservative-enterprise. Each profile defines weights per signal, soft/hard threshold multipliers, and decay windows.
- Tuning workflow: start with conservative-enterprise -> run 100 synthetic canaries -> evaluate false-positive rate and adjust multipliers. Store tuning snapshot with rollout metadata for auditability.
